note: A made-up frame 0 for the tests: six asks, seven principles, five triggers.

asks.text: the service greets each user by name

inversion.the service greets each user by name: the service never greets a user by name

asks.text: greetings can switch between English and Spanish
the greeting style is chosen from presets

inversion.the greeting style is chosen from preset: the greeting style is fixed, with no presets

asks.text: a new preset is added without code changes

inversion.a new preset is added without code chang: a new preset needs code changes

asks.text: the command line reports errors in plain words

inversion.the command line reports errors in plain: the command line reports errors as raw traces

principles.text: A focused fix to what exists comes before a new layer.
Every check reads the requirements, never another check's output.
No generated text reaches the user unchecked.
Nothing edits a greeting after its last check.
A fallback is named, never silent.
The default preset is today's behaviour.
A wrong answer is never shipped as right.

triggers.text: Spending beyond what the human approved goes to the human first.
A change a person sees or presses goes to the human first.
A change to one of the human's decisions goes to the human first.
Anything about the human personally goes to the human first.
A push, a release or a delete goes to the human first.
